extracted.name: Pork & crab 'ants climbing trees'
extracted.description: Make this delicious Sichuan snack made with pork and crab – its name comes from the minced pork that resembles ants climbing trees.
ingredient_lines: 1 medium red chilli deseeded and finely chopped
250g pork mince or minced rehydrated soy pieces
1 tbsp shaoxing rice wine or dry sherry
200g mung bean noodles pre-soaked in hot water for 10 mins, then drained
2 large spring onions ends trimmed, finely chopped
instruction_lines: Heat a wok over high heat and add the rapeseed oil. Stir-fry the garlic, ginger and red chilli for a few seconds, then add the pork mince and stir fry for 2-3 mins until the meat is browned at the edges. Add the rice wine or sherry, season with the dark soy sauce and chilli bean sauce, and mix well. Add the hot stock and bring to a bubble, then tip in the noodles and stir well – keep stirring until all the noodles are coated in the sauce and are a dark brown colour.
Add the crabmeat, gently stir in, and season with toasted sesame oil. Finally, sprinkle in the spring onions, toss well and serve immediately.
